description: Rhododendron stem borer is a beetle whose larvae bore inside plant stems. The larvae tunnel through stems, disrupting water and nutrient flow, which causes wilting and death of branches.
symptoms: Wilting or drooping leaves on individual branches
Small holes on stems where adults lay eggs
favorable_conditions: Presence of adult beetles during spring and summer
Plants with tender stems suitable for egg laying
Gardens or landscapes with susceptible host plants
spread: Adult beetles laying eggs inside plant stems
Larvae developing inside stems and branches
impact: Severe infestations can kill ornamental shrubs
cultural_control: Inspect stems regularly for egg-laying holes
Maintain plant health to reduce susceptibility
biological_control: Encourage natural predators such as birds or parasitic insects
chemical_control: Apply systemic insecticides where infestations are severe
Target adult beetles during egg-laying period
prevention: Regular monitoring during the growing season
Remove and destroy infected stems early
Avoid planting heavily infested nursery plants
